newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai minister refutes rumours of ratings downgrade.
newsitem.headline: Thai minister refutes rumours of ratings downgrade.

text.p: Thai Finance Minister Bodi Chunnananda on Thursday refuted stock market rumours that Thailand's long-term debt ratings may face possible downgrades by Standard & Poor's Corp and Moody's Investors Service.
Bodi told reporters he recently had been informed by Moody's that the credit rating agency would take four to five months to review its long-term rating on Thailand.
Moody's downgraded Thailand's short-term debt rating to Prime-2 from Prime-1 in early September, saying its heavy exposure to short-term foreign debts made it vulnerable to financial shocks.
"There is still no change in Thai ratings. Moody's has asked for time of about four to five months to review Thailand's long-term rating," Bodi told reporters.
The minister said he had also been assured by S&P that the agency would maintain its current rating on Thai long-term debts this year. He did not elaborate.
Rumours of possible Thai downgrades by the two agencies hit the Thai bourse on Thursday, depressing its SET index by about 45.58 points, or 4.29 percent, in mid-afternoon.
